chunks: Nashit ibn Salih narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

“Among the fiqh of the guest is that he should not observe a voluntary fast except with the permission of his host. Among the obedience of the woman to her husband is that she should not observe a voluntary fast except with his permission and command. Among the uprightness, obedience, and sincerity of the servant toward his master is that he should not observe a voluntary fast except with the permission of his master. Among the dutifulness of the child toward his parents is that he should not observe a voluntary fast except with the permission and command of his parents. Otherwise, the guest is ignorant, the woman is disobedient, the servant is corrupt and disobedient, and the child is undutiful.”

key_terms.الضَّيْفِ: the guest whose conduct should respect the host
key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: a voluntary fast, not an obligatory one
key_terms.طَاعَةِ: obedience in a rightful relational duty
key_terms.عَاصِيَةً: disobedient, failing to comply with a required duty
key_terms.فِقْهِ: proper understanding and etiquette in conduct

ai.seo_question: When is voluntary fasting disliked or impermissible without another person's permission in Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out rulings and etiquette concerning voluntary fasting in situations where the rights of others are involved. It teaches that optional fasting should not be undertaken by a guest, wife, servant, or child without the permission of those whose rights are directly affected, emphasizing obedience, courtesy, and the fulfillment of relational duties.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2014 - Nashit ibn Salih narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdullah (as) that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Among the etiquettes of a guest is that he does not fast voluntarily except with the host's permission.

Among the obedience of a wife to her husband is that she does not fast voluntarily except with his permission and instruction. Among the righteousness and obedience of a servant to his master is that he does not fast voluntarily except with his master's permission. Among the dutifulness of a child to their parents is that they do not fast voluntarily except with their parents' permission and command. Otherwise, the guest would be ignorant, the wife disobedient, the servant corrupt and sinful, and the child undutiful."

2015 - رَوَى اَلْعَلاَءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «يُغْتَسَلُ فِي ثَلاَثِ لَيَالٍ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فِي تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ وَ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ وَ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ وَ أُصِيبَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ وَ قُبِضَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ » قَالَ «وَ اَلْغُسْلُ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ هُوَ يُجْزِي إِلَى آخِرِهِ ».
Hadith.2015 - Al-'Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (as)  that he said:
"One should perform the ritual bath (ghusl) on three nights in the Month of Ramadan: the nineteenth, the twenty-first, and the twenty-third. The Commander of the Faithful (as) was struck on the nineteenth and passed away on the twenty-first."
Imam (as) added: "The ghusl should be performed at the beginning of the night, and it suffices until its end."
